chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated from al-ʿAbbās ibn Maʿrūf, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mughīrah, from Muʿāwiyah ibn Maysarah, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام about a man on a journey who does not find water, then prays, then comes upon water while some of the time still remains. Should he continue upon his prayer, or should he perform wudu (ablution) and repeat the salat (prayer)? He said: “He continues upon his prayer, for indeed the Lord of the water is the Lord of the earth.”

The sound understanding of this report is that His saying, “then he prayed,” means that he had entered into the salat (prayer) and had not yet finished it. In that case, it is not obligatory for him to break off; rather, he should continue in his salat (prayer). But if he had already finished his salat (prayer) while time still remained, then repeating it would be required upon him, according to what we have stated earlier.
And what Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated from ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muskān, from Abī Baṣīr, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام about a man who performed tayammum and prayed, then reached water before the time had gone out. He said: “There is no repetition of the salat (prayer) upon him.”
The sound understanding in this as well is the same as what we have stated regarding the earlier reports.

Then he said, may Allah Most High support him: Whoever experiences a seminal emission and fears for himself from ghusl (ritual bath) due to severe cold, or has an illness such that using water would harm him with a harm he fears for himself from, he performs tayammum and prays. Then when ghusl (ritual bath) becomes possible for him, he performs ghusl (ritual bath) for what he will newly begin of salat (prayer).

key_terms.التُّرَابِ: earth, the material used for tayammum
key_terms.السَّفَرِ: travel, the state in which the legal question occurs
key_terms.الْبَرْدِ: cold, a circumstance that may justify tayammum
key_terms.الْغُسْلِ: ghusl (ritual bath), purification required after major ritual impurity
key_terms.الْمَاءَ: water, the normal means of purification
key_terms.تَيَمَّمَ: he performed tayammum, dry ablution in place of water
key_terms.يَتَوَضَّأُ: he performs wudu (ablution), the standard ritual purification

ai.seo_question: If someone prays with tayammum and then finds water before the prayer time ends, must the salat (prayer) be repeated?
ai.summary: This passage discusses the rulings of tayammum when water is unavailable or harmful to use. It explains that one who has entered prayer with valid tayammum continues, and it also addresses the case of illness or severe cold, allowing tayammum in place of ghusl (ritual bath) until use of water becomes possible.
